archetypes.name: Distrustful routine skeptics
archetypes.text: People who say you can't be too careful with others yet still check political information online, and who feel mostly unenthused about politics and democracy while staying pretty happy overall. They report a stalled, below-average family income and see themselves as lower class, but rate the economy as neither good nor bad and keep close ties with relatives. Their unusual mix is strong unease about robots and AI paired with ordinary, mid-level views on science spending and technology, so their worries about automation sit oddly beside their calm, routine outlook on life.

archetypes.name: Distrustful but content loners
archetypes.text: People who report low general trust and skepticism toward institutions and information online, yet feel financially secure and pleased with their own situation. They tend to be disengaged from politics and dissatisfied with democracy while not feeling unhappy in daily life, and they often show mild or strong discomfort with robots and AI taking over human tasks. Their social lives are thin and routine, with infrequent evenings out, and their views on family, technology and science are mixed, with some surprising mismatches between attitudes and everyday habits.

archetypes.name: Distrustful, disengaged, economically strained
archetypes.text: Respondents combine deep distrust of institutions and of other people with low political engagement, yet they actively verify political information online, a pairing that looks contradictory. Financial dissatisfaction and a sense of worsening circumstances coexist with a self-placement in the working class and a view that taxes are too high. Social life is mixed: some describe life as dull or routine while still spending time with friends, and attitudes toward technology and AI are split, with many worried or uncomfortable yet not uniformly opposed.

archetypes.name: Distrustful but upbeat skeptics
archetypes.text: People who distrust others and institutions and feel little connection to politics, yet still describe their finances and personal lives as improving and their days as pretty happy. Their suspicion coexists with contentment, so they rate the economy poorly while personally feeling fine. They are often wary of AI and automation, sometimes deeply uncomfortable with machines doing human tasks, but may be enthusiastic about technology generally. Their social lives are thin, with infrequent friend contact and occasional family visits.

archetypes.name: Satisfied yet distrustful outsiders
archetypes.text: People who are highly content with US democracy and report being very happy, yet hold low trust in other people and in many institutions, and are wary of technology. Their satisfaction with their own finances and the economy sits alongside a sense of being financially behind average families and feeling their income is far below the norm. They lean toward tax resentment and see science as underfunded, while rarely socializing with friends outside their neighborhood or with relatives. The combination of political contentment, personal happiness, and social withdrawal with suspicion of others is unusual.
